summary.text: Youngest son of Neoptolemus and Andromache; he crossed into Asia, slew Areius despot of Teuthrania in single combat for the kingdom, and gave his name to the city still called Pergamon on the Caicus.

story.text: Pausanias names Pergamus third among the sons Neoptolemus begat on Andromache after Troy — after Molossus and Pielus — when the Aeacid settled in Epirus rather than return to Thessaly.

When Molossus received the kingdom in Epirus, Pergamus crossed the sea into Asia, killed Areius, who ruled Teuthrania as a despot and met him in single combat for the throne, and fixed his own name on the city that still bore it in Pausanias' day. Andromache accompanied him, and a shrine to her still stood at Pergamon in Teuthrania.
